cause: Together's google/gemma-4-31B-it endpoint degraded between 2026-08-25T17:06:03Z and 18:17:47Z, producing six transport-uncertain attempts (five request timeouts and one HTTP 503). The strict client recorded each as unknown_charge with its reserved cost held as uncertain spend, deferred the affected cells, and the run continued; every affected cell later completed successfully under a fresh reservation. At the end of formal pass 2, the driver's per-pass accounting (drive_formal -> aggregate_accounting_summary -> validate_ledger) re-applied the zero-uncertain-spend launch rule to the now-live ledger and refused: 'usage ledger contains unresolved uncertain spend'. The driver exited fail-closed at 2026-08-25T18:28:54Z after the pass's final provider call reached its terminal ledger event.

defect_analysis.classification: harness control-plane inconsistency, not a provider or science defect
defect_analysis.detail: Two frozen policies conflict: (1) the in-run transport policy (halt_on_unknown_charge=True at the call level, cell deferral and retry at the run level) deliberately continues the run past billing-uncertain transport failures, holding their reserved cost against the cap; (2) validate_ledger, written as a launch-time gate for a zero-spend fresh ledger, is also invoked by per-pass accounting and by every subsequent driver invocation, and it requires uncertain_spend_usd == 0 and refuses any unknown_charge event. Consequence: the first billing-uncertain transport event after launch makes the run unfinishable and unresumable, with the halt deferred to the next per-pass accounting boundary. Pass 1 survived only because its accounting ran at 17:00:50Z, before the first uncertain event at 17:06:03Z.

A naive relaunch under unchanged code would hit the same inconsistency on the next billing-uncertain transport event, so the inconsistency must be resolved first; the resolution decision is being taken to a Codex consult before any code amendment.
